title: Inferring L1 Backgrounds from L2 English with LLM Token Probabilities
abstract: arXiv:2610.23309v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Native language identification (NLI) infers a non-native speaker's first language (L1) from their second language (L2) production. We investigate a token probability approach that scores each text sample as a continuation of a prompt prefix specifying a candidate L1, then predicts the candidate with the highest score. We evaluate our approach using Llama 3.1 8B and 70B on three datasets: TOEFL9, Write and Improve 2024, and BULATS-L1. We compare its performance with previous prompting-based classification approaches. Token-probability scoring substantially improves on direct classification, particularly with the 8B model, while the 70B model achieves state-of-the-art performance across all datasets. Our results indicate that pretrained LLMs' token probabilities contain information useful for distinguishing L1 backgrounds from L2 English production.

translated_title: 利用大语言模型词元概率从二语英语中推断母语背景
translated_abstract: 母语识别（NLI）旨在从非母语者的二语（L2）语言产出中推断其第一语言（L1）。我们研究了一种词元概率方法：将每个文本样本作为指定候选母语的前缀提示的续写进行评分，然后预测得分最高的候选母语。我们在三个数据集（TOEFL9、Write and Improve 2024 和 BULATS-L1）上使用 Llama 3.1 8B 和 70B 模型对该方法进行了评估，并将其性能与以往基于提示的分类方法进行比较。词元概率评分显著优于直接分类方法，尤其是在 8B 模型上，而 70B 模型则在所有数据集上均达到了最先进的性能。我们的结果表明，预训练大语言模型的词元概率中包含可用于从二语英语产出中区分母语背景的有用信息。
tldr: 提出一种基于大语言模型词元概率的母语识别方法，将文本视为指定候选母语的提示前缀的续写进行评分，显著优于直接分类方法，且 Llama 3.1 70B 在多个数据集上达到最先进性能。
